issues.legal_issue: Reliable and consistent eyewitness evidence may sustain the prosecution case despite investigative omissions, related witnesses, and concurrent findings challenged on appeal.
material_facts: Several eyewitnesses gave consistent accounts of the occurrence, and the courts below found them reliable despite minor discrepancies.
The investigating officer did not collect blood-stained earth or recover the removed crops, but the officer explained the lapse and other evidence supported the place and manner of occurrence.
The accused relied on a counter-complaint, alleged injuries, alibis, and the witnesses’ family relationships; the courts found those claims unsubstantiated or the evidence credible after scrutiny.
The Supreme Court found no perversity or serious infirmity in the concurrent findings about the occurrence.
issues.conclusion: The challenges to the occurrence and the supporting evidence were rejected; the concurrent factual findings did not warrant interference.
issues.legal_principle: Credible eyewitness testimony is not to be discarded solely because an investigative lapse occurred if reliable evidence otherwise establishes the occurrence. Related witnesses are not untrustworthy merely because of their relationship to the victim, but their evidence must be scrutinized with care and caution. In an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution, concurrent factual findings do not call for interference absent perversity or serious infirmity.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and (credible_eyewitness_accounts and (investigative_omissions_are_explained or other_reliable_evidence_supports_occurrence)) and concurrent_findings_are_not_perverse

predicates.criminal_appeal: The accused appealed against criminal convictions and challenged the factual findings supporting them.
predicates.credible_eyewitness_accounts: Witnesses who observed the occurrence gave accounts the courts found reliable after scrutiny.
predicates.investigative_omissions_are_explained: The investigating officer failed to collect or recover some physical evidence but explained the omission.
predicates.other_reliable_evidence_supports_occurre: Evidence apart from the omitted physical evidence supports the occurrence and its location.
predicates.concurrent_findings_are_not_perverse: The trial and appellate courts reached the same factual findings without a demonstrated serious infirmity or perverse approach.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges concurrent findings about an occurrence, reliable eyewitness accounts and supporting evidence may leave those findings undisturbed despite explained investigative omissions.

issues.legal_issue: Severing and moving standing crops with dishonest intent completes theft, and non-recovery alone does not defeat a conviction supported by reliable evidence.
material_facts: The first accused was seen uprooting standing crops from the victim’s family’s field and removing them.
Eyewitnesses described the uprooting and removal, and the investigating officer’s observations corroborated their account.
The crops were not recovered, and there was no substantive proof of their value.
issues.conclusion: The theft conviction was sustained, but the sentence was reduced to one year’s rigorous imprisonment because the value was not substantively proved and time had passed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 378 and 379 of the Indian Penal Code, a thing attached to the earth becomes movable property when severed; moving it to facilitate dishonest taking without the possessor’s consent completes theft. Illustration (a) to Section 378 confirms that the offence is complete upon such severance for that purpose. Non-recovery alone does not defeat a conviction where reliable evidence proves the taking.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and standing_property_is_severed_and_moved and dishonest_taking_without_consent and reliable_evidence_proves_the_taking

predicates.criminal_appeal: The accused appealed against a criminal conviction for taking property.
predicates.standing_property_is_severed_and_moved: The accused severed property attached to the earth and moved it from the possessor’s control.
predicates.dishonest_taking_without_consent: The property was moved with dishonest intent and without the possessor’s consent.
predicates.reliable_evidence_proves_the_taking: Reliable evidence establishes the severance and removal even though the property was not recovered.

issues.definition: When an accused dishonestly severs and moves standing property without consent and reliable evidence proves the taking, the theft conviction may stand despite non-recovery, with the sentence reduced where the value is unproved and time has passed.

issues.legal_issue: Sudden participation in an assault does not establish an unlawful assembly’s common object without evidence of that shared object, though a common intention may arise during the occurrence.
material_facts: The incident began when one accused was caught uprooting crops; the other accused arrived after a commotion and initially sought his release.
The assault began suddenly after the victim refused to release that accused before a village meeting.
The evidence did not establish a shared common object among the accused, but it showed that four accused formed a common intention during the occurrence and joined in acts resulting in the death.
The evidence did not establish that two other accused shared that intention, and the injuries attributed to them were not supported by the medical evidence.
issues.conclusion: The unlawful-assembly and related rioting convictions were set aside. The surviving accused whose common intention and participation were established were convicted of culpable homicide with common intention; the other two accused were not liable for that homicide.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 141, 147, 148 and 149 of the Indian Penal Code require proof of an unlawful assembly and its common object; absent that proof, liability under those provisions cannot stand. Section 34 may apply where a common intention is formed during the transaction and the accused join in the act in furtherance of it. A person cannot be held liable for the resulting homicide merely by association where neither common object nor common intention, nor a causative act, is proved against that person.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and sudden_group_occurrence and no_proof_of_shared_common_object and (common_intention_forms_during_occurrence and accused_join_in_fatal_act or no_proof_of_individual_causative_participation)

predicates.criminal_appeal: The accused appealed against criminal convictions arising from a group occurrence.
predicates.sudden_group_occurrence: Other participants arrived after a sudden dispute and the assault developed at the scene.
predicates.no_proof_of_shared_common_object: The evidence did not prove that the group shared an unlawful common object.
predicates.common_intention_forms_during_occurrence: The evidence showed that some participants formed a common intention during the occurrence.
predicates.accused_join_in_fatal_act: Those participants joined in acts in furtherance of the common intention that resulted in the victim’s death.
predicates.no_proof_of_individual_causative_partici: For other participants, the evidence did not establish a shared intention or a supported act contributing to the death.

issues.definition: In a sudden group occurrence without proof of a shared unlawful object, unlawful-assembly liability is unavailable; homicide liability depends on proven participation in a common intention, and does not extend to those for whom such participation is unproved.

issues.legal_issue: A sudden assault committed without premeditation in the heat of a quarrel may constitute culpable homicide rather than murder, and a common-intention conviction may stand without a specific charge where no prejudice results.
material_facts: The occurrence developed from a sudden dispute after an accused was caught uprooting crops; the other accused arrived during the commotion, and the assault followed the refusal to release him.
The trial court specifically found no premeditation, and the evidence showed that the common intention of four accused arose during the occurrence.
Those four accused joined in acts involving weapons and injuries to vital parts of the victim’s body; the evidence supported an intention to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death.
The accused had been charged on a common-object basis, but the Supreme Court found that the absence of a specific common-intention charge caused no prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The murder convictions based on common-object liability were altered to convictions for culpable homicide not amounting to murder, committed with common intention; the surviving liable accused received ten years’ rigorous imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 300, Exception 4, of the Indian Penal Code excludes murder where culpable homicide occurs without premeditation, in a sudden fight, in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and without undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct. To establish murder under Section 302, the prosecution must also prove that the case falls within one of Section 300’s four clauses. On these facts, Section 304 Part I applied. Section 34 permits joint liability where common intention and participation are proved; failure to charge under Section 34 does not prevent conviction where the accused suffered no prejudice, as stated in Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab (1954 SCR 145).

rule.if: criminal_appeal and no_premeditation and sudden_fight_in_heat_of_passion and no_undue_advantage_or_cruel_conduct and bodily_injury_likely_to_cause_death_is_intended and common_intention_and_joint_participation_are_proved and no_prejudice_from_missing_specific_charge

predicates.criminal_appeal: The accused appealed against convictions for a killing arising from a group occurrence.
predicates.no_premeditation: The evidence and findings showed that the fatal assault was not planned beforehand.
predicates.sudden_fight_in_heat_of_passion: The assault followed a sudden quarrel and occurred in the heat of passion.
predicates.no_undue_advantage_or_cruel_conduct: The circumstances did not show that the offenders took undue advantage or acted cruelly or unusually.
predicates.bodily_injury_likely_to_cause_death_is_i: The participants intended to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death.
predicates.common_intention_and_joint_participation: The evidence established a shared intention formed during the occurrence and joint participation in the fatal acts.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_missing_specific_charg: The accused had notice of the case they had to meet and suffered no prejudice because the specific common-intention charge was absent.

issues.definition: When a killing follows an unpremeditated sudden fight in the heat of passion, without undue advantage or cruel conduct, and the participants jointly act with the requisite intention, the conviction is for culpable homicide with common intention rather than murder if the missing specific charge caused no prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: A demand to release a detained person does not establish resistance to lawful apprehension when the detention was for a village meeting rather than for delivery to lawful custody and no further step was taken to secure release.
material_facts: The victim’s family detained the first accused after catching him uprooting crops and intended to keep him until a village meeting.
Other accused demanded his release, but the evidence showed no further action to obtain his release or to deliver him to police custody.
The prosecution evidence did not establish that the family intended to hand him over to police for lawful custody or action.
issues.conclusion: The convictions under Section 225 of the Indian Penal Code were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 225 of the Indian Penal Code concerns resistance or obstruction to the lawful apprehension of another person, or rescue from lawful custody. A demand for release, without evidence of the relevant lawful apprehension or custody and further conduct establishing the charged offence, is insufficient to sustain conviction.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and demand_to_release_detained_person and detention_is_for_private_village_meeting and no_evidence_of_lawful_apprehension_or_rescue_from_custody

predicates.criminal_appeal: The accused appealed against a criminal conviction for resisting apprehension or rescuing a detained person.
predicates.demand_to_release_detained_person: The accused demanded the release of a person held by others.
predicates.detention_is_for_private_village_meeting: The person was being held until a private village meeting rather than for delivery to lawful custody.
predicates.no_evidence_of_lawful_apprehension_or_re: The evidence did not establish lawful apprehension or custody, or conduct amounting to resistance or rescue.

issues.definition: A release demand does not establish resistance or rescue where the person was held for a private meeting and the evidence does not show lawful apprehension or custody.

issues.legal_issue: Supported convictions for causing hurt with weapons and for simple hurt are not disturbed when the appellate challenge establishes no infirmity in the findings or sentences.
material_facts: The prosecution attributed an assault with a sharp weapon to one accused and assaults causing injuries to other victims to other accused.
The courts below convicted the accused under the provisions addressing hurt with weapons and simple hurt.
The Supreme Court found no substantiated infirmity in the relevant convictions or sentences; the surviving convictions included one for hurt with a weapon and one for simple hurt.
issues.conclusion: The surviving conviction for hurt with a weapon and the surviving conviction for simple hurt, together with their sentences, were confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: A criminal appellate court need not disturb a conviction and sentence where the appellant establishes no infirmity in the findings supporting the offence. The Court applied Sections 324 and 323 of the Indian Penal Code to the respective weapon-caused and simple-hurt convictions.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The accused appealed against convictions and sentences for causing bodily injuries.
predicates.evidence_supports_hurt_conviction: The evidence supports the finding that an accused caused the bodily injury charged.
predicates.no_infirmity_in_conviction_or_sentence_i: The appellant did not establish a flaw requiring appellate interference with the conviction or sentence.

issues.definition: When evidence supports a hurt conviction and the appeal establishes no infirmity in the conviction or sentence, both remain in place.
